cards.explanation: The answer is that he gives generously to the people and prays regularly. Cornelius, the centurion in Caesarea, "…gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly." (Acts 10:2). His faith had open hands and bent knees.

The answer is True. Cornelius "…stared at him in fear…" (Acts 10:4). An angel appears out of nowhere and says your name, and honestly, who wouldn't freeze? I'd have dropped everything I was holding, friends, and I'm a stamper with no hands, so that's saying something.

The answer is that they have gone up as a memorial offering before God. The angel says, "Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God." (Acts 10:4). Cornelius prayed and gave, and the angel tells him those things went up before God. Nothing he did that way was lost along the way.

The answer is Peter. The angel says, "Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter." (Acts 10:5). He goes by two names here, and the angel gives both. That's a handy thing, friends, when more than one Simon is around.

The answer is a tanner. The angel says Peter "…is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea." (Acts 10:6). A tanner is someone who works with animal hides, so I bet that house had a smell you'd remember. That's my own guess, though, because the text only gives his trade and his address.

The answers are servants and soldier. Cornelius "…called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants." (Acts 10:7). So two of the three are household helpers, and Cornelius keeps it close to home. The third traveler is a soldier who is devout, the same kind of man as his boss. I think a man like that is a good one to send on an important trip.

The answer is False. Cornelius "…explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa." (Acts 10:8). He told them about the angel first, and then they hit the road. I think that's a kindness, friends, because nobody likes being sent on a long trip with no reason given.

The answer is pray. Acts 10:9 says Peter "…went up on the roof to pray." While Cornelius's men are walking closer, Peter is already talking to God up there. I like a man who has a spot to go and talk.

The answer is True. Acts 10:10 says that "…while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance." Peter was hungry, and then the trance came right in the middle of the waiting. His stomach was still waiting when everything else changed.

The answer is all kinds of animals and reptiles and birds. The sheet "…contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air." (Acts 10:12). It's a full zoo in a bedsheet, friends.

The answer is that Peter says no and tells the voice he has never eaten anything unclean. Peter answers, "No, Lord!" and then says, "I have never eaten anything impure or unclean." (Acts 10:14). He tells the voice no, right out loud. I think that's a man who has kept this habit his whole life.

The answer is clean. The voice says, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean." (Acts 10:15). It's a short sentence, and Peter has a lot to chew on after it. I'd need a minute too, friends.

The answer is False. Acts 10:17 says Peter was "…puzzling over the meaning of the vision…" Then verse 19 says he "…continued to reflect on the vision…" He didn't get it right away, and he kept thinking about it.
The answer is the Spirit. While Peter is still reflecting, the Spirit speaks up and says, "Behold, three men are looking for you." (Acts 10:19). And He knows the exact number of men at the gate.

The answer is that He has sent the men Himself. The Spirit says, "So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them." (Acts 10:20). The Spirit tells Peter these men aren't random. They are there because He sent them.

The answer is True. The men say Cornelius is "…a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation." (Acts 10:22). They put in a good word for their boss right at the gate. I'd want that kind of reference on my side, friends.

The answer is to bring Peter to his home to hear his message. The men say, "A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you." (Acts 10:22). Cornelius wants to hear what Peter has to say. And he's ready to have him in his home for it.

The answer is that Peter goes with them and some brothers from Joppa. Acts 10:23 says, "…the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa." Peter goes with the three men, and some brothers come along too. Peter doesn't make the trip alone.
